newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.80/2.75 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.90/2.85 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.83/2.78 percent against 2.88/2.83 percent.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.48/98.53 from Tuesday's close of S$98.45/98.50, September 2001 was unchanged from Tuesday's close of S$96.25/96.35 and June 2003 ended at S$94.13/94.18 versus S$94.01/94.06.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 4 3-7/8 percent against Tuesday's 4-3/16 4-1/16 percent.
